title: Desktop window, explicit questions, and lifecycle source walkthrough

files.role: Application-wide WPF templates keep controls theme-aware and switchable between passive reading and deliberate keyboard interaction without introducing an additional content window.

blocks.title: Choose explicit shutdown and resource-driven button behavior
blocks.explanation: The Application has no StartupUri: App.OnStartup constructs and protects the window before showing it. OnExplicitShutdown keeps Hide distinct from Exit and requires the code paths that call Shutdown. Button spacing, minimum height, arrow cursor and semantic brushes are defaults; ControlsFocusable is a dynamic window resource updated by MainWindow.UpdateInteractionControls, not a permanent ban on keyboard access.

blocks.title: Render button state inside its own template
blocks.explanation: Face binds the caller's background, border and padding, while ContentPresenter recognizes access-key text. Hover, pressed, keyboard-focus and disabled triggers use different semantic brush roles; keyboard focus thickens the border rather than creating another window. Replacing brushes in ThemeBrushes.Apply therefore changes these states as well as idle buttons. No opacity reduction is used for disabled button text.

blocks.title: Keep text editing in a plain themed content host
blocks.explanation: The TextBox style removes the app context menu and spell-check UI, forces Arrow, and supplies caret/selection colors. PART_ContentHost is the named ScrollViewer required by WPF text editing; it is not a replacement parser or custom editor. Read-only/focus permissions are assigned by individual controls and code-behind. SelectionOpacity is one, independently of the root background tint.

blocks.title: Theme token entry and list surfaces
blocks.explanation: PasswordBox receives the same cursor, input, text, border and caret roles, but its actual enabled state is controlled by UpdateAudioControls. The default ListBox uses an input-colored background and dynamic ControlsFocusable. The main transcript overrides that background to Transparent in MainWindow.xaml, so these general defaults do not add an opaque layer over the shared tint.

blocks.title: Give ordinary chooser rows visible selection
blocks.explanation: Default ListBoxItem rows start with a transparent border/background and resource-controlled focusability. Hover fills the row; selection fills it with ThemeSelection, outlines it with ThemeAccent and changes foreground. These are chooser/device-list defaults. Main transcript rows use the separate keyed TranscriptRowStyle, whose selection changes only the border, preserving the translucent reading surface.

blocks.title: Draw checkboxes with inline glyphs and focus feedback
blocks.explanation: The two-column template keeps a 14-unit box and check Path beside the content; WPF layout dimensions are device-independent units, not raw screen pixels. IsChecked alone reveals the check; keyboard focus accents the box; disabling changes semantic colors. Dynamic ControlsFocusable allows the same template to serve Wrap and Clarify first in the current interaction mode. The template expresses appearance, not authorization: their click handlers still enforce application state.

blocks.title: Provide a nonfocusable scrollbar track and page actions
blocks.explanation: The vertical scrollbar defaults to width 12 and uses PART_Track with a two-way Value binding and ViewportSize. Transparent repeat buttons retain page-up/page-down command hit areas while the thumb renders a small rounded border. Focusable=False keeps a scroll action from becoming text-entry focus. Opacity zero here belongs to invisible page buttons, not the window or reading text.

blocks.title: Correct commands and dimensions for horizontal scrolling
blocks.explanation: When orientation is Horizontal, the track reverses its direction setting and substitutes PageLeft/PageRight for vertical page commands. A style trigger changes width to Auto and height to 12. Both changes matter to NoteEditor with wrapping off: retaining only the vertical template would give the wrong command direction or a narrow horizontal control.

blocks.title: Make the background slider an actual interactive control
blocks.explanation: The slider has a transparent hit surface, a narrow visual rail, two-way track value, large-step repeat buttons and a styled thumb. It changes MainWindow.BackgroundOpacity.Value; it does not itself set Window.Opacity. The focus resource can be false while pointer interaction remains available, which is how the background control stays useful in passive Present mode.

blocks.title: Render audio meters without independent timers or capture
blocks.explanation: ProgressBar uses PART_Track and PART_Indicator with semantic foreground/background and clipping. WPF supplies the indicator sizing from the control value; the template neither polls hardware nor starts capture. MainWindow's SourceLevelChanged subscriber supplies clamped 0..1 values to the two named meters. The closing resource/application elements complete the document.

files.role: Routes explicit executable modes, establishes same-user single-instance recovery, and owns application-wide failure and shutdown handling.

blocks.title: Enter WPF startup with one owned recovery object
blocks.explanation: Imports cover the specific filesystem/native exceptions caught below. The Application partial retains SingleInstance until exit. OnStartup is an async-void framework override, so its own try/catch is important: ordinary callers cannot await it to receive exceptions. base.OnStartup runs before command dispatch; construction does not rely on a XAML StartupUri.

blocks.title: Prepare explicitly requested answer installation metadata
blocks.explanation: Exact two-argument list patterns select Agency or Copilot preparation. The literal auto becomes null for executable resolution; the resolved path is serialized into answer-setup.json. Copilot also initializes its dedicated profile. Both branches await the metadata write, shut down with zero, and return before single-instance/window startup. These are opt-in command modes, not implicit login or question submission.

blocks.title: Separate capture proof and synthetic UI entry modes
blocks.explanation: Capture proof calls its dedicated RunAsync with transparent=true and propagates its exit code. UI smoke and documentation screenshots create diagnostic MainWindow instances and await RunUiSmokeAsync; the latter requests synthetic device labels with documentationFixture=true. These branches bypass ordinary SingleInstance ownership. Their code describes available execution paths; annotation work does not execute them or establish their results.

blocks.title: Recover the owner or show one protected window
blocks.explanation: A nonowner sends REVEAL through SingleInstance and exits instead of opening another ordinary window. The owner creates MainWindow, registers reveal/status callbacks that marshal through Dispatcher.BeginInvoke, then calls ShowProtected. Recovery therefore reaches RevealAndReset and protection reconfiguration, rather than merely calling Show on an old hidden surface.

blocks.title: Report bounded startup failures without a note-bearing popup
blocks.explanation: The filter names supported native, IO, cancellation, provider and XAML startup failures rather than swallowing every exception. LocalDiagnostics.RecordException records sanitized metadata. Diagnostic modes write a failure receipt with an exception type; only two known synthetic assertion prefixes allow the message into diagnosticDetails. Ordinary failure records a generic LocalFailureNotice and exits with one. Failures while writing that receipt are not separately caught here.

blocks.title: Flush diagnostics before releasing instance ownership
blocks.explanation: OnExit emits ApplicationStopped, asks the diagnostic sink to flush/stop, disposes the mutex/pipe listener owner if one exists, and finally calls the framework base implementation. SingleInstance.Dispose cancels its listener and defers token-source disposal until the listener finishes. This block does not itself dispose audio; MainWindow.Window_Closed owns that chain.

files.role: Records a generic local failure notice when showing a normal error window would undermine the hidden-window failure policy.

blocks.title: Map known failure categories to fixed safe messages
blocks.explanation: WindowFailure distinguishes startup from later capture setup. Record selects fixed text rather than an exception message, note, filename or token; an unknown enum throws. Startup says no notes were loaded, while later setup failure says unsaved text remains in the process. Console.Error receives the same generic notice without opening a WPF dialog.

blocks.title: Persist one timestamped notice with an IO fallback
blocks.explanation: The app creates its LocalApplicationData directory and overwrites last-window-error.txt with UTC ISO timestamp and fixed message. This is a last-error notice, not note recovery or a growing log. IOException and UnauthorizedAccessException fall back to a second generic stderr message. Other failure types remain observable rather than being silently suppressed.

files.role: Exercises the actual answer UI with an in-process stream and synthetic shutdown delegates, without a CLI/model request.

blocks.title: Implement a deterministic streaming and cancellation double
blocks.explanation: The fake captures the AnswerRequest, yields a request-stamped first delta, then signals PartialDelivered with asynchronous continuations. Normal mode waits 50 ms, yields a second delta and explicit completion; cancellation mode waits indefinitely on the supplied token. This arrangement exposes a genuine interval in Streaming state and a cooperative cancellation path, but does not represent real provider latency.

blocks.title: Assert stop initiation ordering and fail-closed configuration
blocks.explanation: BeginConcurrentShutdown is called with capture finishing immediately and provider held by a TaskCompletionSource. The assertion checks call order capture then provider and an incomplete combined task, then releases provider cleanup. An injected InvalidDataException exercises LoadAnswerSettings's SnapshotOnly fallback before installing the synthetic provider. It proves initiation/await composition, not physical device release timing.

blocks.title: Separate frozen request identity from a later edited draft
blocks.explanation: Ask invokes the real UI handler, the fake exposes its first delta, and the test changes questionDraft while the answer is streaming. A second Ask must not increment snapshot count. After awaiting answerTask, it checks the original ExactText reached both request and run, the later text did not, and completion contains the second delta. Screenshot labels explicitly deny a live model response.

blocks.title: Measure synthetic answer-background alpha separately from text
blocks.explanation: Two visual-tree PNGs sample the same DPI-scaled answer-space pixel at 10% and 100% background. The low sample must be nonzero below 60 alpha, the opaque sample 255, and window/text opacity and foreground alpha remain solid. It restores the original slider and renders the illustration. A sampled background pixel and brush checks are narrower than all-pixel contrast or recipient-capture qualification.

blocks.title: Check half-size answer text and reading reachability
blocks.explanation: The fixture reduces the window to its current monitor-dependent minima, yields through Render priority, and checks transcript, draft, snapshot, answer and action reachability plus absence of outer reading scroll. The answer font must be9in the compact minimum layout and10in each of the three additional representative layouts: exactly half the earlier18/20sizes. Those layouts also preserve answer text; original dimensions are restored. These are sampled layouts, not every DPI, font scaling or accessibility configuration.

blocks.title: Cancel a partial answer, reject late state, and report limits
blocks.explanation: A second fake holds after its first delta. CancelAnswer followed by awaiting answerTask must leave Cancelled with the partial text. Applying an event from the first request must return false; because the target run is also terminal, this assertion combines wrong-ID and terminal rejection rather than isolating them. Clear must remove run/text/panel, then provider mode is reset. Failed checks throw; the result's zero-model/no-audio fields describe this synthetic setup.

files.role: Coordinates audio/answer shutdown and the separately owned prepared Agency provider, so slow provider cleanup cannot postpone capture-stop initiation.

blocks.title: Start both cleanup paths and distinguish provider readiness
blocks.explanation: BeginConcurrentShutdown invokes stopCapture first, then stopProvider, before Task.WhenAll awaits either. It does not await all capture cleanup before beginning provider cleanup. ProviderLifecycleBusy tracks preparation/shutdown tasks, while ProviderCanAnswer allows SnapshotOnly, non-Agency modes and diagnostic doubles without Agency readiness. Prepared-provider fields are independent from the current AnswerRun and answerTask.

blocks.title: Gate and coalesce Agency preparation
blocks.explanation: Diagnostics, closing, disabled/non-Agency mode, an active answer, or existing readiness prevent preparation. If shutdown is unfinished, a prepareAfterShutdown latch requests one later attempt; other lifecycle work also blocks duplication. Only after those guards does the method replace the old cancellation source, capture the current settings into PrepareAgencyCoreAsync and refresh controls.

blocks.title: Dispose the old engine before warming an empty session
blocks.explanation: The method clears readiness first, disposes an existing warm provider, checks cancellation, then creates and publishes the replacement before awaiting WarmUpAsync. A second cancellation check prevents a completed-but-cancelled warmup from setting ready. AgencyCliAnswerProvider.WarmUpAsync prepares an empty session, not a model prompt. Readiness status distinguishes default direct Ask from opted-in interpretation.

blocks.title: Keep preparation failure local and refresh after task completion
blocks.explanation: Caller cancellation has a distinct status; provider exceptions preserve the provider's safe code/message; selected infrastructure exceptions produce a generic installation message and type-only diagnostic code. No retry or question send occurs in these catches. The finally queues UpdateAnswerControls because the preparation task may still be incomplete while its own finally executes.

blocks.title: Cancel preparation and serialize provider disposal
blocks.explanation: StopAgencyProviderAsync cancels preparation and clears readiness immediately, returning an already-running shutdown task if present. The core awaits preparation before taking and nulling warmAgencyProvider, then awaits disposal. Recognized cleanup failures set answerProviderClosing, making subsequent PrepareAgencyProvider calls stop instead of silently continuing with uncertain provider ownership.

blocks.title: Release cancellation state and defer requested re-preparation
blocks.explanation: The shutdown finally disposes its preparation token source and schedules a dispatcher callback to update controls and consume a visible-window prepare latch. ReconfigureAgencyAsync awaits shutdown, then prepares only if visible or not yet loaded. This permits startup preparation, not just post-Show preparation; diagnosticRendering suppresses it. A reveal can request warmup, but no path here freezes or submits a question.

files.role: Binds explicit frozen questions to one bounded answer stream, coalesces UI rendering, and preserves incomplete text and identity through cancellation and failure.

blocks.title: Separate settings, run state, task lifetime and rendering cadence
blocks.explanation: Settings begin SnapshotOnly; provider selection, settings validity, current run, cancellation and async task are separate fields. AnswerBusy tests whether answerTask has finished, not whether run.State is Streaming: cancellation can make a run terminal before cleanup completes. The 40 ms DispatcherTimer renders accumulated text, while initialization wires one Tick handler and loads configuration.

blocks.title: Load provider configuration without interrupting owned work
blocks.explanation: Active answer or provider lifecycle work prevents reload. A valid non-SnapshotOnly configuration enables its provider; absent configuration is SnapshotOnly through AnswerConfiguration.Load. Known parse/IO/argument failures reset all three configuration-selection flags to the safe local-only state. Changed configuration resets clarification history. Reconfiguration is then started and controls refreshed; loading settings does not call StartAnswer.

blocks.title: Expose inference location and explicit mode changes
blocks.explanation: ProviderLabel distinguishes GitHub-hosted Copilot, an explicit local model and Agency/model/effort from SnapshotOnly. Snapshot mode refuses a busy answer, clears clarification and stops Agency; configured mode additionally requires valid settings and no lifecycle work, then requests preparation. Reload delegates to LoadAnswerSettings. Selecting a configured provider is not equivalent to selecting a question or authorizing a prompt.

blocks.title: Derive action availability from state rather than captions
blocks.explanation: Controls reflect both answer-task and provider lifecycle state. Notices disclose cloud versus offline-local inference; preparation has its own cancel caption. Ask requires protection, no file/answer operation, provider readiness, nonblank draft and no pending clarification reply. Captions distinguish Freeze locally, Ask provider and Interpret question. Clarification controls are updated last so reply actions share the same current guards.

blocks.title: Keep local freezing separate from starting a provider run
blocks.explanation: SnapshotOnly logs a local freeze, clears any old answer, labels the snapshot unsent and returns. Otherwise a new AnswerRun owns the frozen snapshot and optional clarification metadata, with a fresh request ID used to associate clarification acceptance. Monotonic timing and first-text flags reset per run. RecordContent is an opt-in diagnostics call, not unconditional question logging; the related capture ID comes from source provenance.

blocks.title: Publish run identity before starting asynchronous streaming
blocks.explanation: answerRun is assigned before RunAnswerAsync can yield events. The UI reveals an answer panel, labels exactly what was submitted, replaces the old cancellation source, starts the render timer and stores the new task. Status distinguishes interpretation from solution; EnsureQuestionReadingVisible closes source/setup panels. This order makes incoming work refer to the already-current run and does not alter the underlying draft.

blocks.title: Consume a bounded stream and validate before accepting completion
blocks.explanation: A linked token adds a 120-second UI deadline. The injected diagnostic provider wins; otherwise Agency must be warm, while other configured modes construct CopilotCliAnswerProvider. Each event is checked for cancellation and current run identity/Streaming state before AnswerRun.Apply enforces request and sequence rules. After enumeration ends, cancellation, clarification capacity and explicit AnswerRun completion are checked in that order. Only the current run can update clarification/status; diagnostics separately record received text and completion.

blocks.title: Distinguish user cancellation, timeout and provider failure
blocks.explanation: A cancelled caller token produces Cancelled; a deadline without caller cancellation produces Failed with a 120-second incomplete-text notice. Provider exceptions use their safe message, selected infrastructure failures use a generic one, and neither catch retries. Noncompleted Agency runs clear readiness. The current run's timer stops and renders once more; control reevaluation is queued to the next dispatcher turn because this task is still finishing inside finally.

blocks.title: Render the current answer without claiming pixels were observed
blocks.explanation: The run's text still updates and streams while the workspace is detached. FirstAnswerVisible is logged only when AnswerText.IsVisible, not merely when the outer covered window is visible. The visibility check is outside the text-changed branch so uncovering an already-completed answer records its first visible presentation. This metric remains a visible-control assignment observation, not independently measured rendered or recipient pixels.

blocks.title: Make terminal cancellation immediate but await cleanup separately
blocks.explanation: CancelAnswer logs only a streaming cancellation, transitions the run and cancels its token before rendering the preserved partial text. StopAnswerAsync then awaits answerTask, stops rendering, disposes the token and awaits Agency shutdown. The explicit cancel button records whether work was busy before cancelling: active work schedules reconfiguration, whereas preparation-only cancellation stops Agency without that path.

blocks.title: Copy explicitly and clear without reviving old callbacks
blocks.explanation: Copy refuses empty text and prefixes any noncompleted run with Incomplete answer; clipboard failure leaves memory intact. Clear cancels first, schedules provider reconfiguration, then nulls answerRun, clears/hides the pane, stops the timer and resets clarification. RunAnswerAsync's reference checks prevent an old stream from becoming the visible answer after this nulling, while AnswerBusy still waits for its task to finish.

files.role: Adds an opt-in interpretation/reply state machine while keeping the original question, submitted reply snapshot and completed history distinct.

blocks.title: Represent original, history, request and reply independently
blocks.explanation: clarifyFirst defaults false. clarificationOriginal retains the first snapshot; immutable history records only completed exchanges; clarificationRequestId gates acceptance of a run. AwaitingClarificationReply requires at least one completed interpretation, while ClarificationLocksQuestion begins as soon as an original exists. Thus an initial in-flight or failed interpretation can lock the original without yet exposing a reply.

blocks.title: Toggle without sending and reset before a fresh interpretation
blocks.explanation: Busy answer/file or missing protection restores the checkbox to the real mode and rejects the toggle. A permitted change resets metadata/reply UI, not questionDraft. BeginQuestionClarification first resets, then retains the snapshot and starts an unconfirmed request with empty history. Reset clears original/history/request/answered state and reply text, so switching back to ordinary Ask cannot inherit this conversation.

blocks.title: Expose reply controls only for a completed interpretation
blocks.explanation: waiting swaps the original editor for the reply panel. Reply send requires protection, no file/answer work and provider readiness; corrections are disabled at four interpretations but Yes can still confirm. The Yes button is disabled when a nonconfirmation correction is present. Reply focus/IME additionally require independent questionEditing. Setup displays only this clarification history. Confirmation compares trimmed text to yes case-insensitively; it does not rewrite submitted text.

blocks.title: Reject oversized reply edits without truncating the prior reply
blocks.explanation: renderingClarificationReply suppresses recursive TextChanged during rollback. If the editor exceeds QuestionDraft.MaximumCharacters, the last accepted clarificationReplyText is restored; otherwise the backup advances. Paste evaluates replacement length with a long intermediate and refuses nontext, nonediting or busy-answer cases before insertion. These checks are UTF-16 string-length bounds, not UTF-8 byte limits.

blocks.title: Freeze an explicit reply without replacing the original draft
blocks.explanation: Send uses exactly the reply editor text. Yes refuses to discard a written correction, otherwise submits literal Yes. Submission rechecks state, constructs and validates AnswerClarification from current history, then creates a separate QuestionDraft for this reply and freezes it. lastQuestionSnapshot and the submitted-text panel now refer to the reply; the persistent original questionDraft is untouched. Validation failures report locally and do not send.

blocks.title: Reserve confirmation capacity and accept only the matching run
blocks.explanation: Before completion, unconfirmed output is appended provisionally to metadata and validated as a future Yes request. This enforces per-turn and cumulative limits without silently trimming an interpretation. Acceptance additionally requires current answerRun identity, the stored request ID, opted-in mode and a retained original. A confirmed run unlocks the original; an interpretation appends one completed turn. Reply text clears only on accepted completion, never by automatic submission.

files.role: Tests the desktop clarification controls with synthetic request inspection, explicit corrections and Yes, failure cases and small-window layouts.

blocks.title: Select fake output by typed clarification metadata
blocks.explanation: The provider records every request and selects direct, first-interpretation, corrected-interpretation or confirmed-answer text from AnswerRequest.Clarification. Oversized mode emits 8193 characters; hold mode waits indefinitely on cancellation. Each stream stamps one delta and completion with the same request ID and increasing sequence. This tests UI protocol/state handling, not whether a real model follows interpretation instructions.

blocks.title: Prove opt-in does not itself submit and original text remains locked
blocks.explanation: The fixture clears prior state, records default-off from both backing field and checkbox, installs a fake Agency provider, toggles on and asserts zero requests. Ask sends the deliberately garbled original exactly once with unconfirmed empty history. After awaiting completion it checks interpretation heading, one history entry, original preservation and the awaiting-reply state.

blocks.title: Check reply reachability and protect a written correction
blocks.explanation: Three sizes, including actual minima, yield at Render priority and emit layout receipts. Reply editor, send, confirm and answer must be reachable without an outer reply scroll. After restoring size, independent typing enters a correction but must not send. Calling Yes with that correction must preserve it and request count; replacing it with 8193 characters must restore the correction rather than truncate. At each representative size it also enters actual reply-edit mode and checks that the reply editor and Send reply remain readable; this catches longer Done typing/Copy original labels wrapping the action row and stealing reply height.

blocks.title: Send corrections and confirmation only on explicit actions
blocks.explanation: Send reply must include the correction as ExactText and the original/first interpretation in history, while questionDraft remains original. Typing spaced mixed-case Yes still sends nothing until the click; the request preserves those spaces and case while metadata becomes Confirmed. Completion restores the original editor. Toggling clarification off and Asking again must send original text with null metadata and empty local history.

blocks.title: Exercise cancellation and an interpretation too large for history
blocks.explanation: A held stream prevents changing clarification mode; the handler restores the checkbox. Cancel must produce Cancelled with no completed history and retain original text. After clear, an 8193-character fake interpretation fits the larger answer buffer but must fail clarification-result validation, leaving history empty. This distinguishes answer-output capacity from the smaller per-interpretation history contract.

blocks.title: Verify local-only fallback and aggregate synthetic assertions
blocks.explanation: With the fake still installed but useAnswerProvider=false, Ask freezes the original locally without increasing provider requests or entering reply state. The fixture clears/reset controls and removes its fake, then combines every check and verifies no transcriber is running. It writes clarification.json and throws on failure. Zero model requests and no recording are fixture declarations, not live provider/device qualification.

files.role: Connects the desktop to bounded local diagnostics, reports sink health, and labels the boundary when opening its folder outside the protected window.

blocks.title: Keep monotonic correlation and diagnostic health state
blocks.explanation: The source-level timestamp dictionary supports the main constructor's one-per-second meter diagnostics. Capture/request start timestamps and first-answer flags distinguish received from assigned text. A two-second DispatcherTimer monitors log health; it is not the 40 ms answer rendering timer and does not poll an audio input. IO, hashing and JSON imports are used by initialization and folder actions below.

blocks.title: Load text-logging consent and identify the executable safely
blocks.explanation: ReloadSettings resets text logging before parsing in LocalDiagnostics; known settings failures keep metadata logging and show a generic status. SHA256 of the running assembly, truncated to 16 hex characters, identifies the build rather than hashing notes or filenames. Failure to read that assembly gives a local status and leaves build null. ApplicationStarted also records whether this is diagnostic rendering.

blocks.title: Surface dropped or unwritable logs without hiding application data
blocks.explanation: Each health tick checks the sink's FailureCode and shows a generic permissions message when needed. The Diagnostics button includes DroppedRecords only when positive. The timer starts once during MainWindow construction and is stopped in Window_Closed. A clean later tick updates the count caption but does not explicitly clear a previously reported StatusText message.

blocks.title: Open diagnostic storage only on a deliberate click
blocks.explanation: The click reloads current settings, creates the known diagnostics directory and asks the shell to open it with UseShellExecute. Status discloses whether text logging was explicitly enabled and that the folder is outside capture protection. Known IO/JSON/shell failures leave an inline generic error. Opening this folder is not an upload or a diagnostic probe.

files.role: Fits the single window to monitor work area and allocates readable transcript/question/answer space without wrapping the workspace in an outer scrolling surface.

blocks.title: Recover usable bounds before revealing a window
blocks.explanation: ClampWindowToWorkArea uses RestoreBounds when minimized, otherwise current requested geometry. First placement or explicit recenter passes null coordinates to WorkspaceLayout.FitToWorkArea; later placement preserves position when it fits. Returned minima are applied before size/location so small work areas can reduce the normal minimum. workspacePositioned records that initial centering has occurred, then reading layout is refreshed.

blocks.title: Report requested protection and convert monitor pixels to WPF units
blocks.explanation: The status intentionally says requested, not verified invisible. Work-area lookup falls back to SystemParameters.WorkArea when no HWND or monitor information exists. MonitorFromWindow uses nearest-monitor behavior; successful native rectangle corners are converted through TransformFromDevice before producing a WPF Rect. This avoids treating physical monitor pixels as logical window coordinates.

blocks.title: Allocate wide columns or a constrained stacked reader
blocks.explanation: After readiness guards, width selects WorkspaceLayout's900-unit columns threshold. Short workspace is height below780or transcript area below500. Narrow short layouts may replace transcript space with source tools or clarification replies. PartialText now uses10.5units in compact Q/A and13.5otherwise, exactly75%of its former14/18sizes. Final transcript text is15units in XAML. AnswerText remains9compact/10normal and question typography is unchanged. Row-padding equality avoids redundant resource replacement. Audio setup hides the transcript while its full-area card panel is open. Cover and host-switching states skip layout mutation of the detached workspace; normal layout is recalculated after uncovering.

blocks.title: Keep submitted text readable without crowding a clarification reply
blocks.explanation: A short workspace hides the submitted snapshot while awaiting a reply, but does not erase lastQuestionSnapshot. Otherwise short layouts pair draft and snapshot in columns; tall layouts allocate a separate snapshot row. The draft row receives extra weight for replies. Visibility changes trigger layout recalculation. EnsureQuestionReadingVisible closes the chooser and provider details before recalculating, keeping controls inside the same visual tree.

blocks.title: Mutually exclude source and provider tools, with inline protection details
blocks.explanation: Source expansion hides provider setup and updates both captions. Provider toggling first collapses sources and then applies its own new state. Each calls UpdateWorkspaceLayout because tool height changes reading allocation. Protection Details independently toggles an inline panel and caption rather than creating a popup whose protection would need separate treatment.

blocks.title: Define the exact synthetic notion of reading reachability
blocks.explanation: The helper raises minimum height for TextBox line height/padding/borders and for transcript ListBox row padding. It rejects hidden, narrower-than-24 or too-short controls, then checks window coordinates and the lower boundary at NotesToggleButton, with one-unit tolerance. HasOuterReadingScroll walks visual ancestors for ScrollViewer. These geometric predicates do not inspect glyph contrast, actual occlusion by another app or screen-reader usability.

blocks.title: Declare monitor structures and native lookup signatures
blocks.explanation: Sequential layouts match the native rectangle and monitor-information fields: size, full monitor/work rectangles and flags. The caller initializes Size before GetMonitorInfoW. Return-value Bool marshaling and MonitorFromWindow/GetMonitorInfo imports are the interop boundary; this code does not enumerate every monitor or persist placement across application restarts.

files.role: Drives real local-question handlers with synthetic transcript events and records exact-text, independent-focus, stale-session and layout assertions.

blocks.title: Check clamped default sizing and exact newline preservation
blocks.explanation: The fixture enters Present if needed, compares current size to WorkspaceLayout's monitor fit, and labels synthetic/no-audio status. It edits and freezes LF, CR and CRLF inputs through the actual Ask handler and requires the displayed editor text and frozen ExactText to agree without normalization. QuestionClear then gives subsequent selection tests fresh state. This path runs under the smoke harness's SnapshotOnly setup.

blocks.title: Select one provisional microphone segment without implicit Ask
blocks.explanation: A fixed new session contains unselected computer and microphone finals plus one microphone partial. The chooser is filtered to Mic, its realized row receives a synthetic preview click, and Use selected copies only that segment. Assertions check unchanged foreground, PassiveWindow and zero new snapshots. Explicit Ask then freezes the partial; a later final updates the live draft but must leave the submitted snapshot text unchanged.

blocks.title: Prove question focus does not cancel audio startup or admit old events
blocks.explanation: The fixture substitutes a start token and audioBusy flag, enters/exits question typing, and checks notes remain read-only, token uncancelled and native NoActivate restored. This models lifecycle guards without opening a device. After a manual edit, unrelated speech and a stamped old-session final must not alter the question or admit stale transcript text. An overlimit editor assignment must roll back to the prior draft.

blocks.title: Assert reading brushes and smallest supported geometry
blocks.explanation: Theme switches must preserve question text. Across every UiTheme, eight reading controls must use the expected HighContrastReading color with brush/control opacity one. At current MinWidth/MinHeight, transcript, draft, snapshot and question actions must satisfy geometric reachability, and draft/snapshot must lack outer ScrollViewer ancestors. Rendering/layout receipts provide inspectable geometry, not live capture evidence. The primary Ask action is also checked across every theme and at the minimum layout for right alignment, size, separation and accent/action-text brushes.

blocks.title: Retain selection and HWND across layouts, then test destructive boundaries
blocks.explanation: The minimum layout first requires final/partial font sizes15/10.5; three additional representative layouts require15/13.5, proving the requested25%reduction from20/14/18. Those layouts must preserve HWND, draft, note and selected structured keys while keeping controls reachable. Clear replaces question identity/snapshot without erasing transcript/notes; empty Ask does not increment its count. Direct-selection checks and no running transcriber remain mandatory. Every responsive size also repeats primary-action geometry/brush checks.

blocks.title: Check the actual primary-button template and placement
blocks.explanation: The helper measures Ask and Clear in the shared action grid. Ask remains large in column2; Clear must occupy column3 at least eight units beyond Ask, with its right edge aligned to the grid. It resolves ClearFace and requires the actual ThemeError brush and a two-unit border. Secondary edit/copy controls must remain left of Ask, and Ask still uses the palette accent/action-text pair. Theme and responsive loops exercise this combined geometry/color contract without submitting a model request.

blocks.title: Record control geometry alongside a synthetic visual-tree image
blocks.explanation: The named control array covers chrome, transcript, tools, draft, snapshot, answer and reply actions. Each record translates its origin to window coordinates and includes dimensions, visibility, the reachability predicate and outer-scroll result. JSON is followed by RenderDiagnosticAsync for the same state. These receipts diagnose layout decisions; they do not measure recipient video frames or claim every visible glyph was inspected.

files.role: Owns the live structured question model, local draft/snapshot and independent typing transition, including the manual chooser path and explicit Ask/copy/clear actions.

blocks.title: Start with a local draft and a separately identified transcript session
blocks.explanation: questionTranscript and questionDraft are independent of display/export TranscriptBuffer. The chooser defaults to Mic but selects nothing automatically. PassiveWindow means presenting AND not questionEditing; HasQuestionContent also counts a snapshot or any answer run for exit warnings. Initialization creates a session, binds main transcript rows, enables rendering/selection synchronization and expands Q/A. It does not freeze or send a question.

blocks.title: Expand Q/A without confusing visibility with activity
blocks.explanation: Collapsing Q/A cancels the current answer and starts Agency shutdown; if typing was enabled, it returns to passive question mode. Expanding closes Notes/audio setup, keeps partial text visible, updates layout and requests eligible provider preparation. This method does not stop transcription. ResizeQuestionPanel delegates to the shared workspace allocator rather than maintaining an unrelated size policy.

blocks.title: Filter the chooser by structured source and preserve matching keys
blocks.explanation: Mic/Computer/All set a nullable AudioSource filter; RefreshQuestionSegments enumerates nonempty structured records, remembers currently selected keys and restores those still in the filtered view. Button borders indicate the filter. In passive mode a preview row click toggles selection and marks the event handled instead of relying on WPF focus. This chooser click alone does not populate the draft; Use selected is separate.

blocks.title: Make manual chooser replacement deliberate and atomic
blocks.explanation: Clarification locks reject replacement; no selected keys preserves the existing draft. Otherwise selected keys filter the store in its order and QuestionDraft.ReplaceSelection validates/copies the complete set before rendering. This explicit replacement path does not include the direct-click UserEdited guard: Use selected can deliberately replace corrections. It also lacks the direct handler's protection/fileBusy checks, so those must not be advertised as identical code-level guards.

blocks.title: Refresh only the selected question as recognition changes
blocks.explanation: AudioSource defaults to Computer for missing source metadata. Partials/finals enter StructuredTranscriptStore with the already-checked capture GUID, source, protocol identity and timing. Unless clarification locks the original, QuestionDraft.Refresh upgrades selected nonfinal keys only and never overwrites a user-edited draft. Draft-capacity failure reports preservation but still refreshes chooser and display; it is distinct from invalid transcript failure handled by ReceiveTranscript.

blocks.title: Take question keyboard focus without the global Notes transition
blocks.explanation: Entering typing requires no file operation and valid protection; repeated state is a no-op. With protection, it hides first, changes questionEditing, updates focus/IME controls and reapplies protection on reveal. It never calls StopVisibleActivityAsync. Only nondiagnostic deliberate entry focuses the original or reply editor. Done typing restores PassiveWindow when still presenting. Focus changes and re-protection are real side effects even though no audio-stop or Ask occurs.

blocks.title: Derive original-editor permissions and copy semantics
blocks.explanation: The original editor is writable/focusable only during questionEditing and outside a clarification lock; IME follows that exact focusability. The edit action changes caption to Type reply while waiting and stays disabled during an initial locked interpretation. Copy targets original draft text, so its caption becomes Copy original while waiting. UpdateAnswerControls refines the provisional Ask-enabled state using provider/busy/clarification rules.

blocks.title: Protect the original from locked edits and reject oversized paste
blocks.explanation: Programmatic rendering is ignored. A clarification lock immediately re-renders the original instead of accepting changed text. Otherwise QuestionDraft.EditText validates before mutation and RenderQuestionDraft restores prior state on failure, not truncated input. Paste requires typing mode and UnicodeText, and computes post-selection replacement length in long arithmetic against the 8192 UTF-16-unit bound. Actual TextChanged remains the backstop for locked or other input paths.

blocks.title: Render model text with provenance while suppressing recursion
blocks.explanation: renderingQuestion guards model-to-control TextChanged recursion. Text is assigned only if it differs; provenance reports revision, UTF-16 length, provisional state, user-edit protection and explicit source count. Controls and direct transcript highlights are then synchronized to the model. The finally always clears the rendering flag, including when downstream updates throw.

blocks.title: Freeze once only after Ask preconditions succeed
blocks.explanation: Waiting-for-reply blocks a duplicate original Ask; an active answer or unready provider blocks before snapshot creation; protection/fileBusy are checked next. Freeze captures current draft text/provenance, increments the diagnostic counter and displays that immutable text. It calls BeginQuestionClarification only for opted-in provider use, otherwise StartAnswer (whose SnapshotOnly branch sends nothing). Known input/provider validation failures report inline without silently retrying.

blocks.title: Copy only the draft and clear question state independently
blocks.explanation: Copy rejects an empty draft, writes only questionDraft.Text to the clipboard and reports ExternalException without loss; reply text is not substituted. Clear first cancels/clears answer and clarification, then creates fresh draft state, drops last snapshot, empties its panel and chooser selections, and re-renders direct highlights. Transcript and note stores are deliberately untouched; clipboard copying is explicit but outside capture-affinity protection.

files.role: Connects whole displayed transcript rows to immutable structured identities for direct multi-click question composition without parsing display labels.

blocks.title: Keep display decoration separate from selectable segment data
blocks.explanation: TranscriptRow pairs DisplayText with an optional TranscriptSegment. IsSelectable is false exactly when no segment exists, which disables session separators through the XAML keyed style. Observable main rows and a replaceable partial array have distinct lifetimes. renderingTranscriptSelection suppresses recursive SelectionChanged events when the model deliberately updates highlights.

blocks.title: Append only new final display text and archive unfinished rows
blocks.explanation: Unchanged TranscriptBuffer length means no row is added, covering empty/duplicate finals. A new row pairs the newly appended display slice (minus the trailing platform newline) with the current session's matching final structured segment. Scrolling follows only if already within one unit of the end. At a new session, partial rows are paired with their closed structured revisions and labelled unfinished; a null-segment separator is display-only.

blocks.title: Rebuild partial rows and reconcile selection by identity
blocks.explanation: Active nonempty partials are sorted by AudioSource and displayed with source labels, but retain the structured segment alongside the label. ItemsSource replacement is guarded against selection recursion. SyncTranscriptSelection projects draft keys into both lists, clearing/readding highlights under the same guard. A selected partial can therefore become a final with the same key without losing its selection merely because the row object changed.

blocks.title: Toggle whole rows and roll back disallowed edits
blocks.explanation: A realized enabled row consumes the preview click and toggles IsSelected, with no Ctrl requirement. SelectionChanged ignores rendering recursion, then rejects missing protection, fileBusy, a manually edited draft or a clarification lock. It can open Q/A to explain the refusal, but restores highlights from the unchanged model. Direct clicks are not promised passive: the successful branch below explicitly enters question typing.

blocks.title: Compose selected raw segments in view order, not click order
blocks.explanation: The key dictionary starts from copied draft entries, then applies removals/additions. Main rows followed by current partial rows determine visible ordering; selected entries outside the view are retained before those rows. ReplaceSelection atomically enforces one session, 256 keys and 8192 UTF-16 units. Success renders, opens Q/A, closes tools, enters independent typing and synchronizes the smaller chooser. Failure restores highlights and preserves the draft; no Freeze or provider call occurs here.

blocks.title: Locate the actual list scroll viewer in the visual tree
blocks.explanation: The recursive helper returns the first ScrollViewer at or beneath a visual, stopping on a match. AppendFinalTranscriptRow uses it to preserve a user reading earlier history; synthetic tests use it to inspect scroll offsets. It searches rendered WPF children, not files, text or semantic transcript content, and returns null when no such viewer exists.

files.role: Uses synthetic routed row clicks to exercise direct multiselection ordering, identity, provenance retention, draft guards and scroll preservation.

blocks.title: Arrange adversarial labels and click in reverse history order
blocks.explanation: A new session contains a multiline Mic row whose raw text includes [Computer], then equal-text Computer and Mic rows with different identities. Q/A closes, audioBusy and a cancellable startup guard simulate active startup, and the second row is clicked before the first. Assertions require raw history-order composition, correct structured sources, deliberate question editing, preserved notes/export, no new snapshot and an uncancelled startup token. No actual capture is running.

blocks.title: Distinguish duplicate text and protect frozen/manual state
blocks.explanation: Adding equal text must create a third selected identity, and toggling either row must remove only its own key. After restoring ordinary audio flags, explicit Ask freezes the multiselect text; later deselection must not rewrite the snapshot or add another. A manual editor correction makes a subsequent direct click fail and restore highlights. Clear question must remove selections from both main and partial lists.

blocks.title: Follow a selected partial through finalization and store eviction
blocks.explanation: Selecting one live partial must preserve selection as text revises and move the highlight to the final row when its key settles. Adding 260 finals evicts that key from the 256-entry chooser while the main row and copied draft survive. An older main row remains selectable. Scrolling to the top followed by new partial/final events must keep the reading position, testing follow-end rather than unconditional autoscroll.

blocks.title: Reject capacity, busy, protection and cross-session additions
blocks.explanation: An 8193-character row is valid transcript text but cannot enter the smaller question draft. After selecting a valid row, oversized, file-busy and protection-not-ready clicks must preserve its draft/highlight. A new session's separator must be ignored and its final cannot mix with the old selection. Clearing the question then selecting an archived partial must retain its raw text, provisional status and inactive identity.

blocks.title: Clear transcript while retaining copied draft and report twenty checks
blocks.explanation: Setting exportedTranscript to the current export permits ClearTranscript_Click; it must empty rows/partials without erasing the already-copied unfinished question. The fixture then creates friendly synthetic rows for subsequent screenshots. Twenty named assertions are combined, written to transcript-selection.json with zero-model/no-recording declarations, and throw on failure. The guard simulation and routed events do not qualify real microphone hardware or human interaction.

blocks.title: Stimulate the real routed-event selection path
blocks.explanation: ClickTranscriptRow scrolls the chosen row into view and forces layout so virtualization creates a ListBoxItem. Missing realization throws rather than silently skipping the test. It raises a Mouse.PreviewMouseDownEvent on that container, reaching the registered preview handler and SelectionChanged logic. This is stronger than assigning questionDraft directly, but still synthetic rather than physical mouse input.

files.role: Defines the one native WPF workspace, inline tools and independent reading surfaces; its resource bindings and event wires are part of the capture, focus and explicit-action design.

blocks.title: Declare one layered native surface and its local resources
blocks.explanation: The existing Window remains transparent, tool-window-style, nonactivating by default and responsible for its caption, resize and lifecycle events. Window.Resources now begins with device-card templates; no new native popup or browser surface is introduced.

blocks.title: Render each device as a selectable card
blocks.explanation: The ListBoxItem style inherits dynamic focusability and supplies a bounded default card, margin and padding. The automation name binds the full friendly name. A radio dot and accent outline indicate selection; hover/focus and disabled states are local template changes. The control still owns the original RenderDevice or MicrophoneDevice record, so styling never replaces the endpoint ID.

blocks.title: Remove scrolling from the device control itself
blocks.explanation: The list uses a nonvirtualizing WrapPanel and an ItemsPresenter inside a clipped Border, with no ScrollViewer in its template. Both scrollbar properties are explicitly disabled. Friendly names wrap and can ellipsize in an exceptionally constrained card; only presentation is abbreviated. Page changes collapse off-page containers rather than replacing ItemsSource or clearing SelectedItem.

blocks.title: Retain the separate transcript row template
blocks.explanation: TranscriptRowPadding and the raw DisplayText template remain independent of device cards. This template renders already-associated transcript rows with high-contrast text; device paging does not modify transcript selection or parse its source labels.

blocks.title: Show direct selection without painting over translucent reading space
blocks.explanation: The keyed row style uses dynamic focus/padding and a permanently transparent background. Hover, selection and keyboard focus change only outline brushes, with a three-unit leading edge. IsSelectable=False disables separator rows through a data trigger. This intentionally differs from App.xaml's general chooser style, whose selection fills a background; direct rows retain solid high-contrast text over the shared tint.

blocks.title: Retain native caption/resize regions and clickable header actions
blocks.explanation: The caption retains native drag/resize behavior and client-hit-testable actions. The title reserves46units on the left for the separate32-unit book icon; the normal right-side action cluster returns to a five-unit margin. WorkspaceHost still detaches the main visual/logical content without removing the mask toggle.

blocks.title: Expose semantic themes and bounded background tint
blocks.explanation: Theme buttons use separate icon/label/current-name elements updated by ApplyTheme. The slider starts at 55, bounds values to 10..100, snaps in five-point steps and binds its numeric readout. ValueChanged targets only BackgroundOpacity_ValueChanged, which changes WindowSurface's brush alpha. The toolbar's ThemeSurface remains opaque and the slider remains pointer-usable in Present mode.

blocks.title: Keep unsaved-content decisions inside the existing surface
blocks.explanation: ConfirmPanel starts collapsed and offers save notes, export transcript, explicit discard and cancel with an Edit/copy hint. It is an inline Border using warning colors, not a modal secondary WPF window. RequestActionAsync decides when it appears; the separate confirmation handlers decide whether saving/exporting actually clears all relevant dirty categories before continuing.

blocks.title: Separate capture actions from input-mode choice and meters
blocks.explanation: Start/Stop, setup, export and Q/A visibility have distinct event handlers. Computer/Mic/Both buttons choose mode but do not start capture. Two 0..1 ProgressBars identify PC and Mic independently; the heading and labels are presentation, not audio source parsing. Stop/export begin disabled, while UpdateAudioControls derives runtime availability from protection and lifecycle flags. A12-unit red ellipse beside the heading uses ThemeError with a solid high-contrast outline. Hidden reserves its space while stopped, avoiding action-row movement. It is noninteractive and has an accessible recording-state name; visibility comes from actual transcription running state, not selected input mode.

blocks.title: Keep capture status outside the setup workspace
blocks.explanation: AudioStatus remains in the top transcription control area after moving device setup into the reading region. Errors and capture state therefore stay visible while selecting devices; the closing StackPanel ends the shared heading and input-mode section.

blocks.title: Give final transcript rows their own scroll and selection surface
blocks.explanation: TranscriptArea has named columns/rows mutated by UpdateWorkspaceLayout. Its main ListBox uses15-unit text,25%smaller than the earlier20, with Multiple selection, transparent fill, solid reading text, disabled horizontal scrolling and pixel-based virtualized vertical scrolling. Both preview clicks and SelectionChanged are wired, so pointer and other selection paths converge. The overlaid placeholder is not hit-testable and cannot intercept deliberate row selection.

blocks.title: Keep live partials selectable and clarification opt-in
blocks.explanation: PartialText is a second Multiple ListBox with13.5-unit italic text,25%smaller than its earlier18-unit default. Responsive compact mode uses10.5instead of14. It retains its own scroll, identity-aware template/handlers and82-unit height bound before responsive adjustment. The transparent Q/A panel is initially beside transcript, with separate source/provider toggles and an unchecked ClarifyFirstToggle. No XAML trigger here submits a request.

blocks.title: Preserve a manual source chooser distinct from direct clicks
blocks.explanation: The collapsed QuestionSourcePanel offers Mic/Computer/All filtering and a separate Use selected action. Its 76-unit Multiple ListBox shows TranscriptSegment.DisplayText, wraps text and routes passive clicks to QuestionSegments_PreviewMouseLeftButtonDown. Unlike the main transcript it has no SelectionChanged-to-draft event: selection alone is not replacement. The automation name explicitly describes this no-auto-send boundary.

blocks.title: Disclose provider/provenance details beside explicit question actions
blocks.explanation: The collapsed details panel holds the inference-location notice, SnapshotOnly/configured/reload controls, draft provenance and run label. ClarificationContextText is a read-only, separately scrollable history display rather than the original question editor. A configured provider label wraps instead of forcing the workspace wider.

blocks.title: Separate left editing tools from the primary Ask action
blocks.explanation: The star-width left column contains only Type/edit and Copy, with four-unit horizontal padding so their longest labels fit the minimum window while replying. An eight-unit spacer separates the right action group. Ask remains in column2,148wide/minimum44high with15-unit semibold text and ThemeAccent/ThemeActionText. Its wrapping label and border-based hover/focus/press feedback preserve mode changes and colored fill; disabled state dims the face. The final Auto column is reserved for Clear, not another send action.

blocks.title: Place Clear after Ask with a persistent red outline
blocks.explanation: Clear uses column3, a98-unit width and the same44-unit minimum height. Its six-unit left margin plus Ask margin provide separation. The border binds ThemeError with thickness2, giving a red outline in every theme. Hover, keyboard focus and press change only the neutral face background, so generic button accent-border triggers cannot replace the red outline. Disabled state dims the face. The original QuestionClear_Click handler is unchanged: this is relocation/styling, not a new data-loss or provider action.

blocks.title: Give original question and clarification reply different text controls
blocks.explanation: QuestionReadingGrid starts with draft, optional snapshot and answer row weights. QuestionEditor accepts multiline text but is initially read-only/unfocusable and delegates validation to TextChanged/Pasting instead of truncating with MaxLength. The collapsed reply panel has its own editor, hint and explicit Send reply/Yes buttons. Separate storage is what allows a correction or Yes request without overwriting the original draft.

blocks.title: Display immutable submitted text separately from mutable input
blocks.explanation: QuestionSnapshotPanel starts collapsed, participates in layout on visibility change and contains a read-only nonfocusable multiline text box with transparent fill. Its label is changed by StartAnswer to distinguish local freeze from actual submission. A separate answer-placeholder TextBlock collapses when AnswerPanel becomes visible. Neither displayed snapshot nor placeholder is a second editable question source.

blocks.title: Keep streamed answer, actions and failure status in the same reader
blocks.explanation: The answer grid has fixed-action and status rows around a star-sized plain-text reader. Its default FontSize is10WPF units, half the former20; responsive layout uses9instead of18when compact. Cancel and Copy remain above it while AnswerText scrolls internally with transparent fill and fully opaque high-contrast glyphs. RenderAnswer changes the heading to INTERPRETATION as needed, so that same field inherits the smaller type. QuestionStatus remains a separate bottom row for draft/request actions.

blocks.title: Give device selection the complete reading area
blocks.explanation: The opaque inline AudioPanel spans both reading columns/rows and initially stays collapsed. It uses existing visibility coordination to close question/notes panels, not another HWND. The header explains direct selection and page-based overflow; a star-sized devices region absorbs remaining space instead of pushing controls below the window.

blocks.title: Keep Computer and Mic identity and paging separate
blocks.explanation: Each source has its own title, Refresh action, card ListBox, explicit empty message and fixed-height previous/page/next strip. Both lists retain the passive click handler, and selection/size callbacks update page presentation. The output and microphone pager handlers cannot borrow the other source's selected object. Accessibility names identify each list and paging direction.

blocks.title: Keep service setup available without crowding device cards
blocks.explanation: Service setup, Clear transcript and Done remain reachable beneath the cards. The token field and prior edit/privacy guidance live in a collapsed advanced section; missing-token Start opens it explicitly. The password remains session-only and disabled outside the existing Edit/idle policy. Closing setup restores the reading view without saving, clearing or automatically recording anything.

blocks.title: Keep notes collapsed and file/find actions inside the surface
blocks.explanation: NotesToggle and generic DocumentStatus occupy a stable separator used by reachability tests. NotesSection starts collapsed with toolbar, optional inline find and a 140-unit editor row. FileToolbar starts disabled; global Edit enables it. Wrap defaults on and font/find actions are explicit. FindText and its Next/Close buttons do not create an auxiliary search dialog.

blocks.title: Use a plain read-only-by-default note editor and hide empty status
blocks.explanation: The note TextBox accepts returns/tabs, preserves an undo limit of 100, offers both scroll directions and uses a transparent background with opaque reading text. ReadOnly and Focusable are later controlled by global Present/Edit, not question typing. Paste and TextChanged route to validation/dirty tracking. A text trigger collapses StatusText only when its string is empty, avoiding permanent blank status height.

blocks.title: State capture limitations without claiming universal invisibility
blocks.explanation: The footer shows pending/requested protection and a recovery shortcut, plus an inline Details toggle. The initially collapsed detail text explicitly limits screen sharing, recording, pickers, cursor, accessibility and OS indicators; these are not inferred safe from native affinity. Closing elements finish the one-window visual tree. The shell's protection setup does not extend to arbitrary external file dialogs or diagnostic folders.

blocks.title: Keep a plain book cover and one recovery action outside the workspace
blocks.explanation: The cover contains NOTEPAD IS READY and the same always-mounted icon-only toggle at the top left. A small original vector book Path replaces text captions, avoiding icon-font or image dependencies. The button's32by32target is explicitly client-hit-testable inside the caption; the title is offset to leave room. Meaningful accessible names still describe the action, but no Cover/Uncover caption is drawn. The same HWND and continuing-work lifecycle are retained.

files.role: Coordinates the window's protection, focus, notes, explicit audio lifecycle, transcript display and synthetic UI harness; other partials share this state rather than forming independent windows.

blocks.title: Keep preservation baselines and lifecycle flags independent
blocks.explanation: Imports identify WPF/native, file, diagnostics, audio and Core dependencies. savedText/exportedTranscript are comparison baselines, not autosave buffers; documentPath/fingerprint/BOM describe the current note. Present, DeepSeaFoam and Both are initial choices, but protectionReady and audio activity begin false. Distinct fileBusy, audioBusy, audioStopping, stop task, close guard and start cancellation fields prevent conflating UI mode with asynchronous ownership.

blocks.title: Initialize resources before controls and marshal audio callbacks
blocks.explanation: The public constructor delegates to diagnosticMode=false. Diagnostic mode is set before initialization so provider preparation can be suppressed. ControlsFocusable and theme brushes exist before InitializeComponent resolves dynamic resources, then diagnostics/questions/answers initialize in order. The service token comes from environment into PasswordBox. Transcript/status/fault subscriptions dispatch to WPF; a fault records metadata, stops capture, restores the fault message and zeros meters rather than silently switching inputs. Device-card collection/generator listeners are initialized after InitializeComponent, before normal device discovery.

blocks.title: Update source-specific meters with rate-limited metadata
blocks.explanation: Each SourceLevelChanged callback chooses Mic or Computer meter, clamps the level to 0..1 and records at most one diagnostic per source per elapsed second. The recorded integer is normalized level times 10000, not PCM samples or transcript content. Construction then enumerates devices and derives control state; enumeration is not a StartAsync call and does not imply capture began.

blocks.title: Configure the native surface before showing it
blocks.explanation: showing brackets reconfiguration so its own display messages do not trigger invalidation. protectionReady is false until WindowProtection.Configure returns; placement/minimized state is repaired next. On first HWND setup, a hook, two hotkeys and session/power subscriptions are installed. ShowActivated follows PassiveWindow except in diagnostics. Controls update before Show, status says protection requested, then eligible Agency preparation starts. finally clears showing even if setup throws.

blocks.title: Provide recovery when a hotkey conflicts or protection fails
blocks.explanation: A hotkey collision is caught independently and points to second-launch recovery; it does not abort window creation. RevealAndReset recenters before TryReveal. TryReveal reruns ShowProtected and activates only deliberate nonpassive, nondiagnostic modes. Recognized native/protection failure starts InvalidateAsync, which hides before its first await, and writes a generic local CaptureSetup notice. There is no fallback to unprotected display.

blocks.title: Handle owned-window cursor, hotkey and nonactivation messages
blocks.explanation: Dispatch queues actions only while dispatcher shutdown has not started. The HWND hook handles WM_SETCURSOR for this window with a fixed Arrow; WM_HOTKEY dispatches hide/recover or forced global Notes Edit. Passive WM_MOUSEACTIVATE returns 3 (MA_NOACTIVATE), which permits pointer interaction without ordinary activation. Display/DPI changes outside ShowProtected queue invalidation. These local messages do not control a recorder's cursor layer.

blocks.title: Hide first on observed session, power or protection invalidation
blocks.explanation: Lock/logoff/remote-connect/disconnect and suspend/resume notifications marshal invalidation. InvalidateAsync immediately clears protectionReady and questionEditing, hides the window and cancels the answer before awaiting StopVisibleActivityAsync. Its status is stored after cleanup and requires deliberate recovery to see. These notifications cover detected transitions, not every external recorder change or a guarantee against frames already captured.

blocks.title: Distinguish Hide and global Notes Edit from question typing
blocks.explanation: Hide clears questionEditing, hides/cancels and awaits visible-activity shutdown; recovery uses TryReveal. TogglePresentationAsync first rejects fileBusy, computes Present/Edit, hides and stops audio/answers before changing mode. Entering global Edit expands Notes and focuses NoteEditor only after successful nondiagnostic reveal. This is intentionally not SetQuestionEditing: routing question typing through this method would stop transcription.

blocks.title: Derive focus, file permissions and dirty categories
blocks.explanation: ControlsFocusable follows !PassiveWindow, but NoteEditor writability/focus/IME follow !presenting, so question editing can focus controls while notes stay read-only. File/export controls require global Edit and no file operation. Audio/question updates refine their own controls. Thin click handlers enter asynchronous action methods. NotesDirty compares full current text to savedText; TranscriptDirty compares a nonempty export to its last explicitly saved content.

blocks.title: Queue destructive actions and preserve pending intent during IO
blocks.explanation: New/Open require global Edit and all actions reject fileBusy. Exit first stops visible activity, then pending is set; dirty notes always prompt, while transcript/question content prompt on Exit. ExecutePendingAsync rechecks fileBusy before clearing pending or hiding confirmation. Exit permits Close; New resets file identity, BOM, saved baseline, editor and undo history; Open delegates to the file picker. A blocked replacement keeps both current note and pending action. Exit first uncovers so its existing unsaved-content confirmation remains visible, then follows the normal audio/provider shutdown path; Cover alone never invokes it.

blocks.title: Require all exit preservation categories to be resolved
blocks.explanation: Save notes continues only after success and, for Exit, no dirty transcript or remaining question content. Export similarly requires clean notes and no remaining question content on Exit. Therefore saving one category is not permission to discard the others; even copied question state still needs an explicit clear/discard decision. Discard executes pending directly; Cancel clears pending and collapses confirmation without replacing content.

blocks.title: Commit an opened note only after strict read succeeds
blocks.explanation: The single-file native picker is cancelable and precedes fileBusy. NoteFileStore.ReadAsync performs bounded strict UTF-8 decoding and fingerprinting; only after it returns are path/fingerprint/BOM/saved/editor fields replaced. Toggling undo clears prior-document history. Known file errors retain the existing document and give a generic 1 MiB/access hint. finally reenables controls. Native picker surfaces are explicitly outside capture-exclusion assurance.

blocks.title: Select save destination without treating dialog cancellation as success
blocks.explanation: Save refuses Present mode and concurrent file work. Existing document path/fingerprint are reused for ordinary Save; Save as or a new document opens a generic .txt SaveFileDialog with overwrite prompt. Cancel returns false before setting fileBusy. A newly selected destination resets expected fingerprint; the following block reads an existing destination before writing so replacement can still check for intervening changes.

blocks.title: Advance the saved baseline only after persistence completes
blocks.explanation: fileBusy disables editor changes and content snapshots the exact text being saved. Save-as/new overwrite reads the destination fingerprint, then NoteFileStore.WriteAsync verifies it around a same-directory temporary write. Successful return updates path/fingerprint/savedText. A NoteConflictException has its own Save as guidance; other known failures retain edits with an access/space/UTF-8/size message. finally always clears busy. The helper's checks are conflict detection, not an external-writer lock.

blocks.title: Keep note status generic and validate the full paste result
blocks.explanation: File failure classification covers IO/access/encoding/argument exceptions. SetFileBusy disables the editor and confirmation panel before recalculating actions. Dirty status reveals neither path nor note text and explicitly says no automatic saving. Paste obtains UnicodeText, constructs the post-selection replacement, and asks NoteFileStore.Fits to enforce strict UTF-8 bytes including any BOM; invalid/nontext/Present paste is cancelled, not truncated.

blocks.title: Change font and root tint without fading glyphs
blocks.explanation: Note font steps by two within 12..42. Background alpha is rounded from clamped 10..100 percent times 255/100 and assigned to WindowSurface.Background using current theme RGB; Window.Opacity and reading control opacity are untouched. ApplyTheme replaces resources, updates next-theme icon/name/automation text and Plain outline, then reapplies the existing slider value so switching palettes preserves tint strength.

blocks.title: Toggle notes without erasing them and find from current selection
blocks.explanation: Expanding Notes hides audio setup and collapses Q/A (which cancels/stops its provider); collapsing only hides Find. Wrap changes TextWrapping without changing content. Find opens the inline panel; Next rejects empty input, searches after the current selection with current-culture case-insensitive matching, wraps once to the beginning, and selects/scrolls the match or reports none. Visibility changes do not reset note text or undo state.

blocks.title: Reserve Escape for question typing and shortcuts for global Edit
blocks.explanation: Escape first exits independent question typing and consumes the event. Other shortcuts are ignored unless exactly Control is held and presenting is false, so question typing during Present does not gain note Open/Save/New commands. Ctrl+S/O/N/F are marked handled and routed to their existing guarded asynchronous/file/find methods rather than duplicated implementations. While covered, only Tab, focused-toggle activation and normal Alt+F4 routing remain; hidden workspace editing/file shortcuts are consumed.

blocks.title: Refresh Computer and Mic lists independently
blocks.explanation: Existing selected device IDs are saved before enumeration. Each successful list replacement reselects the same ID or the first available item, and empty lists provide mode-specific guidance. Separate catches let one discovery succeed when the other fails; the second status can supersede the first. This refresh does not substitute an input in an active session: RefreshDevices_Click below rejects active startup/running/stopping states.

blocks.title: Keep passive device choice local and audio tools inline
blocks.explanation: Refresh is blocked while starting, running or stopping. In Present, a click on an enabled device-row container assigns its Content directly to SelectedItem and consumes the preview event, avoiding the default focus-requiring ListBox click path. Audio setup toggles inline; opening it collapses Notes/Q&A but does not start audio. This is passive device choice, unlike direct transcript selection's deliberate typing transition.

blocks.title: Reject explicit Start before disturbing session state
blocks.explanation: Duplicate Start during busy/stopping/running returns immediately. Capture mode determines which selected device objects are required; protection, every requested input and a token length of at least 32 are prerequisites. Failure exposes audio setup with an Edit/token hint. The endpoint defaults to literal IPv4 loopback and must parse as absolute before audioBusy/session changes. Stronger loopback/path validation follows inside the try; URI parsing alone is not the network policy. A missing token expands the inline Service setup section so the existing setup guidance still leads to a visible password field.

blocks.title: Start a GUID-stamped capture with old partials archived
blocks.explanation: A local cancellation source is published so Stop can cancel startup; controls enter audioBusy before work. After ValidateEndpoint, the display buffer begins a session, a new capture GUID/timestamp is recorded, the structured store closes old partials and ArchiveTranscriptPartials materializes their history rows. StartAsync receives only selected device IDs, endpoint, token and that GUID. Known failures show generic startup guidance; finally clears the published token reference/busy flag before the using scope disposes it. Preparation is not rolled back into the old session.

blocks.title: Disable source changes throughout startup and stopping
blocks.explanation: Start requires idle plus protection; Stop is available while starting or running but disabled during stop. Both device lists and mode buttons use a shared idle predicate. Mode determines visible/enabled sections and label/border, while token entry additionally requires global Edit. SetCaptureMode repeats the busy guards, so directly invoking its handler cannot bypass disabled buttons; successful mode changes only reset meters and controls, never open inputs. UpdateRecordingIndicator reads transcriber.IsRunning on every controls refresh, so starting/buffering alone does not light the red icon and stopped/faulted state hides it.

blocks.title: Coalesce repeated stops and cancel startup before waiting
blocks.explanation: StopTranscriptionAsync returns the existing incomplete audioStopTask. Otherwise it sets audioStopping and disables changes, cancels any pending start token, then stores StopTranscriptionCoreAsync. The core awaits transcriber.StopAsync and records elapsed capture time; recognized connection/device failures warn that unfinished tail text may be missing. finally clears stopping, zeros both meters and recalculates controls, independent of whether stop reported an error.

blocks.title: Reject stale capture callbacks before mutating either transcript
blocks.explanation: A production event without CaptureSessionId becomes Guid.Empty; only diagnostics may borrow the current session for synthetic events. A mismatched GUID returns before logs or data updates. Accepted partial/final events update display/export buffer, then structured question state, then final/partial UI rows and placeholder.
