Finals require segment IDs. Known invalid data or capacity failures stop transcription and retain memory for export. Updates across the two stores are sequential, not a multi-store transaction.

blocks.title: Export one transcript snapshot without autosaving audio
blocks.explanation: Export requires global Edit, no file work and content; the native .txt picker is explicitly cancelable. Once busy, transcript.ExportText snapshots finals plus any unfinished labels. Existing destination fingerprint is read before bounded NoteFileStore.WriteAsync; only success advances exportedTranscript. Capture is not stopped by export, so later transcript changes can make it dirty again. Failure keeps in-memory text, and finally releases fileBusy. This exports text, not PCM.

blocks.title: Clear transcript only after full stop and saved export
blocks.explanation: Running, startup-busy and stopping states all reject Clear. Dirty transcript also rejects it with export-or-discard-at-exit guidance. Success clears display and structured stores, chooser and export baseline, then clears main rows under a selection-recursion guard and refreshes partials/placeholder. It intentionally does not call questionDraft.Clear: copied question text can outlive clearing the source transcript.

blocks.title: Serialize close requests and release window-owned subscriptions
blocks.explanation: Until allowClose is explicitly granted, WPF Closing is cancelled and at most one queued async Exit request proceeds. Its finally clears the queue guard even when a prompt keeps the window open. Closed unsubscribes system events, removes the HWND hook, unregisters hotkeys, stops diagnostic health and sets answerProviderClosing before awaiting visible-activity and transcriber disposal. Application.Shutdown is explicit after cleanup; this differs from Hide.

blocks.title: Set up a synthetic UI harness without enabling inference
blocks.explanation: RunUiSmokeAsync creates its output directory, forces diagnostic rendering and invalid SnapshotOnly provider state, then reveals through the normal protection path. It measures foreground/native passive state, Start availability, default notes collapse and Both selection. The token is cleared and endpoint counts recorded. Documentation mode replaces displayed device names with synthetic fixtures; constructor enumeration already happened, but no capture start is implied.

blocks.title: Populate synthetic source rows and inspect local cursor/nonactivation
blocks.explanation: Fixed notes plus Computer/Mic finals and partials exercise the real ReceiveTranscript path using diagnostic session fallback. Source labels must appear in both row collections. After rendering, transcript-primary geometry is checked. Native WM_MOUSEACTIVATE and WM_SETCURSOR messages verify MA_NOACTIVATE and Arrow policy along with control cursor properties. These messages cannot establish that a remote recorder includes or excludes the cursor.

blocks.title: Check theme bindings and preserve original content/handle baselines
blocks.explanation: The harness snapshots note/export/HWND and iterates every UiTheme, checking actual dynamic resource colors and note/transcript reading brushes against ThemePalette. It renders each theme, tests Plain-to-dark-to-light button transitions/icons, restores DeepSeaFoam and renders audio setup. These are specific brush/state assertions; they do not compute all contrast ratios over arbitrary backgrounds.

blocks.title: Exercise passive Computer and Mic device-row clicks
blocks.explanation: Two synthetic devices replace each real enumerated ItemsSource temporarily. After layout, a preview mouse event on the second container must change selection without making the row focusable or changing foreground/Keyboard.FocusedElement. Original list and selection are restored after each source. This tests the shared passive handler against actual realized WPF containers, not device capture or real pointer automation.

blocks.title: Use busy/stopping negative controls before any audio can start
blocks.explanation: Computer and Mic modes must enable/hide the corresponding device sections. With audioBusy=true, attempting a mode change must retain Both. With audioStopping=true, invoking Start, mode change and Clear must leave the export unchanged and Start/mode controls disabled. These flags deliberately simulate transitional states; the assertions do not require or prove WASAPI startup/shutdown behavior.

blocks.title: Sample low/full root alpha and check solid foregrounds
blocks.explanation: The fixture renders at 10% and 100%, converts a transcript background point through current DPI and reads one Pbgra32 pixel alpha. It requires a nonzero low alpha below 60, opaque alpha 255, full control/window opacity, opaque foreground brushes and unchanged HWND. Reset to 55 follows sampling. A local RenderTargetBitmap is evidence about the WPF visual tree only, not screen-capture exclusion.

blocks.title: Exercise notes expansion, internal scrolling and native hit regions
blocks.explanation: Notes expansion must keep presenting true. One hundred synthetic transcript rows drive an internal vertical scroll, then the real row collection/highlights are restored under the render-selection guard. A long unwrapped note tests horizontal scrolling before text/wrap restoration. WM_NCHITTEST samples must return caption=2, left resize=10 and client=1 at the editor, separating drag/resize from text interaction.

blocks.title: Check global mode permissions and block busy document replacement
blocks.explanation: The real presentation toggle must enable note editing on request and restore read-only/nonfocusable Present while leaving the tint slider enabled. Repeated mode/Notes visibility transitions must preserve notes/export. Setting fileBusy and pending New then executing must leave both note and pending action intact. Finally minimizing and RevealAndReset must restore a normal visible-state window after protection reapplication.

blocks.title: Force URI rejection before transport or device work
blocks.explanation: The diagnostic substitutes a Computer device and synthetic 64-character token so missing-input/token guards do not mask the URI branch. It temporarily sets an invalid URI, invokes Start_Click and throws unless the inline invalid-address status appears. finally restores environment, clears the token, restores device items/selection and returns to Both. This tests early validation only, not endpoint connectivity.

blocks.title: Combine synthetic subdiagnostics and close even on failure
blocks.explanation: Question, answer, clarification and recording-indicator diagnostics are awaited; each throws on failed assertions before final receipt generation. The outer passed expression combines shell/layout/theme/guard checks, tool-window style and no running capture. result.json includes individual booleans, API readback, discovered counts, fixture mode and an explicit no-real-audio/no-remote-cursor-guarantee limitation. Return is zero or two; finally grants close regardless of success. Recorded invalidUriRejected=true is justified by the preceding throw-on-failure branch. The audio-device-card diagnostic is also awaited, including paging/selection, busy locks, empty state and compact Service setup. The cover diagnostic additionally checks continued fake streaming/transcript callbacks, detached fresh automation traversal, cached-reference limits and workspace restoration.

blocks.title: Render WPF content locally and pack native hit-test coordinates
blocks.explanation: RenderDiagnosticAsync updates layout, yields to Render priority, scales dimensions by actual DPI and renders the window into Pbgra32 before PNG encoding to the requested file. It is not a screenshot of the user's desktop. HitTestDiagnostic converts a WPF point to screen pixels and packs signed-coordinate low/high 16-bit fields for WM_NCHITTEST; SendMessage/GetForegroundWindow declarations support the synthetic native assertions.

files.role: Applies and checks the shared Windows arrow cursor only in the app's owned-window cursor-message path.

blocks.title: Load a shared Arrow handle and reject native load failure
blocks.explanation: The static Arrow value uses LoadCursor with null instance and integer resource 32512. A zero handle throws Win32Exception using the preserved last error instead of silently using a missing cursor. SetArrow assigns this handle and IsArrow compares current cursor handle for diagnostics. MainWindow.WindowMessage calls SetArrow for its own HWND; no ShowCursor loop or global cursor visibility modification exists here.

blocks.title: Declare the narrow user32 cursor boundary
blocks.explanation: LoadCursorW requests last-error preservation because loading can fail. SetCursor and GetCursor use native pointer-sized handles; the code does not inspect another process or manipulate a recording product. The loaded system cursor is shared rather than created by this class, so no owned-cursor destruction path is declared.

files.role: Provides session-local instance ownership and a narrow same-user REVEAL recovery channel without accepting arbitrary text, paths or executable commands.

blocks.title: Derive a per-user name and acquire local-session ownership
blocks.explanation: Current Windows user SID is required, hashed with SHA256 and shortened to 24 hex characters for the pipe/mutex suffix. The mutex name has the Local namespace prefix; IsOwner follows whether this invocation created it. The pipe itself uses the SID-derived name, while CurrentUserOnly is applied by streams below. The hash names the channel; it is not an authentication secret or a universal cross-session mutex guarantee.

blocks.title: Send only REVEAL and start one listener
blocks.explanation: A nonowner creates a same-machine, output-only, asynchronous CurrentUserOnly client. Connect/write/flush share a five-second cancellation source and exactly six UTF-8 command bytes. Listen rejects nonowners and a second listener, then stores the async loop task. App.OnStartup supplies dispatcher-marshalled callbacks, so the IO loop need not manipulate WPF controls on its own thread.

blocks.title: Read a bounded command from one same-user connection
blocks.explanation: The loop creates one input-only byte-mode server instance with CurrentUserOnly. After connection, a linked two-second request timeout bounds ReadExactlyAsync into a six-byte buffer. Only those bytes matching REVEAL invoke the callback; any other six-byte value gets a generic rejection. The implementation does not inspect trailing bytes beyond the command, so it should not be described as validating the peer's entire stream.

blocks.title: Separate listener shutdown from peer timeout and connection failure
blocks.explanation: Cancellation caused by shutdown exits quietly; other cancellation reports a request timeout and accepts another connection. IOException reports a generic recovery failure and delays 250 ms before retrying to avoid a tight error loop. That delay also observes shutdown. These error messages reveal no incoming bytes, user SID, note content or file path.

blocks.title: Release the owner mutex without disposing a live listener token
blocks.explanation: Dispose is idempotent, cancels listener work, releases the mutex only for its owner, then disposes the mutex handle. If no listener exists it disposes shutdown immediately; otherwise a default-scheduler continuation disposes it when the task ends. This avoids disposing the cancellation source beneath pending pipe IO and does not block application exit waiting synchronously for a dispatcher callback.

files.role: Registers and releases only this window's explicit Ctrl+Alt recovery/edit hotkeys, without installing a keystroke hook.

blocks.title: Record only successfully registered hotkey IDs
blocks.explanation: The primary constructor captures the HWND. Visibility and editing IDs are separate from virtual keys supplied by MainWindow (Space and E). Register combines Control, Alt and NoRepeat bits; native failure throws immediately with last error, and only success appends the ID for cleanup. MainWindow catches collisions and leaves second-launch recovery available.

blocks.title: Attempt every unregister and keep cleanup diagnostics generic
blocks.explanation: Dispose walks successfully registered IDs and calls UnregisterHotKey on the captured handle. A failed unregister emits a generic Trace warning but does not prevent later IDs being attempted; clearing the list makes another Dispose harmless. Both interop declarations preserve last error and marshal Win32 BOOL; only registration uses last error to throw.

files.role: Applies native tool-window/nonactivation styles and capture affinity, retaining readback uncertainty rather than converting API success into a recorder guarantee.

blocks.title: Require a supported desktop and obtain a hidden-capable HWND
blocks.explanation: ProtectionResult records readback availability, nullable affinity and error separately. Constants identify extended styles and WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE=0x11. Configure refuses Windows earlier than build 22000, calls EnsureHandle without needing Show, checks DWM HRESULT and composition state, and throws if unavailable. MainWindow controls visibility/order; this native helper does not load notes or independently hide the window. DisallowPeek is the documented DWM attribute11, distinct from capture affinity0x11.

blocks.title: Preserve other style bits and distinguish missing from contradictory readback
blocks.explanation: The existing extended style is read-modify-written: ToolWindow added, AppWindow removed, NoActivate set or cleared by the requested interaction mode. SetWindowPos uses no-size/no-move/no-zorder/no-activate plus frame-changed flags. Affinity setter failure is fatal; successful getter with a value other than 0x11 is also fatal. Getter failure alone is retained in ProtectionResult. DwmFlush submits composition synchronization, not independent recipient-capture qualification. The same HWND also receives DWMWA_DISALLOW_PEEK=true as a32-bit BOOL. A failing HRESULT follows the existing hidden protection-failure path. PeekPreventionRequested means setter acceptance, not observed shell preview or universal capture exclusion.

blocks.title: Handle zero native return values correctly across process bitness
blocks.explanation: Get/SetWindowLongPtr are used for 64-bit and Get/SetWindowLong for 32-bit. Last error is cleared before each call because a zero old style/value can be legitimate; only zero with a nonzero last error throws. The 32-bit write checks conversion to int instead of silently truncating. FlushComposition maps DwmFlush's HRESULT to a managed exception.

blocks.title: Declare the exact user32 and DWM contracts
blocks.explanation: Pointer-sized and 32-bit entry points are separate imports with last-error preservation. Affinity and SetWindowPos return Win32 BOOL and are explicitly marshalled; DwmIsCompositionEnabled returns HRESULT plus a marshalled Boolean, and DwmFlush returns HRESULT. These signatures express local API setup only: they neither inspect a sharing application's backend nor verify captured pixels.

files.role: Declares the Windows WPF executable and its Core/audio dependencies; build metadata does not qualify the resulting UI or package.

blocks.title: Select the desktop executable target and manifest
blocks.explanation: Microsoft.NET.Sdk plus UseWPF makes App.xaml/MainWindow.xaml compiled WPF resources/code. WinExe selects a GUI executable, net10.0-windows and EnableWindowsTargeting identify the platform target, and ApplicationManifest points to app.manifest. AssemblyName is PhantomFudge and declared package/assembly version is 0.1.0. Repository Directory.Build.props supplies nullable/implicit-usings/warnings/determinism/lockfile settings; nothing here demonstrates a build was run.

blocks.title: Reference the domain layer and the external audio package
blocks.explanation: The ProjectReference makes Core models, file store, answer adapters and policies available to the WPF app. NAudio is pinned at 2.2.1 and used by the Audio subdirectory, a different atlas ownership boundary. The package's internal implementation and lockfile are not interpreted by this desktop annotation; this block states the declared dependency, not device compatibility.

files.role: Translates Core's semantic color strings into WPF resources, including control system-color overrides and the separate high-contrast reading role.

blocks.title: Replace semantic resource brushes from a single palette
blocks.explanation: Apply reads ThemePalette.For(theme), maps each color field to the matching Theme resource name, and replaces resource entries with frozen brushes. The palette Name is presentation text, not a brush. HighContrastReading is distinct from ThemeText so white/black reading text can coexist with canonical muted/chrome colors. DynamicResource consumers in App/MainWindow XAML observe these replacements; arbitrary hardcoded brushes would not follow this mapping.

blocks.title: Align built-in colors and freeze parsed brush instances
blocks.explanation: System control/window/highlight/gray resource keys point at the same semantic objects, keeping framework-rendered pieces coherent with custom templates. Color uses WPF ColorConverter; Brush constructs a SolidColorBrush and freezes it before returning, so theme switching replaces immutable instances rather than mutating shared ones. MainWindow calls Color separately when constructing a per-slider alpha background.

files.role: Shows the active transcription state as a protected red icon and exercises its presentation without opening audio inputs.

blocks.title: Map active transcription to an inline recording icon
blocks.explanation: The partial window uses WPF visibility and the existing palette. The small setter makes the icon Visible only for the supplied running state and Hidden otherwise. Hidden retains its layout slot, so recording transitions do not move Start/Stop. Production calls it from UpdateAudioControls with transcriber.IsRunning; it does not infer recording from sound levels, partial text or the chosen Computer/Mic/Both mode.

blocks.title: Check stopped, starting and active presentation without audio
blocks.explanation: The diagnostic saves busy/status/theme state and first requires no running transcriber and a hidden icon. It models startup with audioBusy=true, refreshes production controls and requires the dot to remain hidden. Only the view setter is then driven with true across all themes, checking visibility, exact theme-error brush, solid opacity and12by12dimensions. No capture object is started or its Running field changed.

blocks.title: Render a disclosed synthetic example and restore state
blocks.explanation: The example uses the original theme and an explicit SYNTHETIC status saying no inputs opened. After visual-tree rendering, false must hide the icon. finally restores busy/status/theme and refreshes controls even if rendering fails. The aggregate also requires the real transcriber to remain stopped. A failed assertion throws; recordingStarted=false describes the fixture, not a hardware recording experiment.

files.role: Coordinates measured card rows and source-independent overflow pages while preserving endpoint selection.

blocks.title: Observe source collections without replacing selected objects
blocks.explanation: Each source owns an independent page index, capacity and reveal-selection flag. Collection and generated-container events queue layout after the actual records exist. The lists and their selected endpoint objects remain the source of truth; the helper owns only presentation. These listeners are attached to controls owned by this window, not global device hooks.

blocks.title: Coordinate the setup workspace and selected-page reveal
blocks.explanation: Only a true visible transition closes Notes and Q/A and asks each list to reveal its selection. A parent hide does not recursively reenter the question-edit transition. Service setup toggles inline, while size and selection changes request a reflow. A selection marks only that source's page for reveal; no input is opened by any of these handlers. While Cover swaps hosts, visibility callbacks do not close Q/A or cancel provider activity; the normal explicit audio-setup transition retains its existing behavior.

blocks.title: Coalesce layout work and keep source modes separate
blocks.explanation: A queued flag and arranging guard prevent recursive reflow while dimensions or visibility are changing. Work is dispatched at Loaded priority and skipped while the setup panel is closed or not initialized. The group grid uses two columns for Both and one for a single source; empty-state notices and each independent list's layout are then refreshed. finally releases the arranging guard on every path.

blocks.title: Measure friendly-name cards within real viewport dimensions
blocks.explanation: Unrealized or very small/invisible lists wait for a later layout rather than using bogus dimensions. Columns derive from a190-unit target; width reserves margins. FormattedText measures wrapped friendly names with actual font/DPI, starting at68units high and adding content padding. The height is bounded by available space, so exceptionally long names may use the template's ellipsis without altering identity. Unexpected item types fail explicitly.

blocks.title: Compute finite pages without losing hidden selections
blocks.explanation: The calculation first tests capacity without a pager, then reserves32units only when pages are needed. Capacity is columns times whole rows and never zero. RevealSelection maps the existing selected index to its page; otherwise the current page is clamped. The label also shows where the selected device lives. Paging changes container visibility/geometry only, preserving ItemsSource and SelectedItem even when that card is temporarily hidden.

blocks.title: Reject browsing while capture lifecycle locks inputs
blocks.explanation: Output and microphone arrow handlers route to their own page objects. Disabled lists, startup, stopping or active capture reject navigation with an inline message. An accepted arrow changes only a page index and reflows cards, never selects another device automatically. Direction comes from the two declared button tags; there is no model or audio transport interaction.

files.role: Exercises actual no-scroll card templates and source selection using synthetic device records only.

blocks.title: Settle WPF geometry and reject hidden scrolling or clipped cards
blocks.explanation: The diagnostic performs three bounded layout/queued-update passes. Its geometry predicate rejects any ScrollViewer in the device-list template, checks every visible card's edges against the list, and requires at least one visible card for a nonempty collection. It checks container fit, not that arbitrary-length device names can always be displayed without ellipsis.

blocks.title: Populate a disclosed large synthetic device catalogue
blocks.explanation: The fixture saves original selections, sources, size, mode, status and theme. It substitutes23playback and17microphone records, selects the first of each and opens setup with service details collapsed. Minimum, medium and large viewports must keep visible cards inside both lists and keep the lists themselves reachable. No capture device is constructed or started.

blocks.title: Page without selecting, then explicitly select a card
blocks.explanation: At minimum size the Next action must advance the output page while retaining the previously selected object. A synthetic preview click on the first visible card then selects that exact output, leaves the microphone unchanged and preserves passive foreground behavior. Every theme must render the selected card's actual accent border; the compact screenshot is synthetic evidence only.

blocks.title: Cover capture locks, single-source layouts, service setup and empty lists
blocks.explanation: A busy flag disables both lists and paging and must reject a navigation attempt. Computer-only and Mic-only views use a full-width source column while retaining identity. Expanded service details must remain usable without card scrollbars. Empty catalogues must show explicit messages and remove pager strips; absence is not fabricated into a selectable default device.

blocks.title: Restore controls and report only synthetic scope
blocks.explanation: finally restores dimensions, original item sources/selections, mode/status/theme, closes setup and restores Q/A even if a check fails. The aggregate requires all geometry, selection, style, lock, mode, service and empty-state checks plus a stopped transcriber. It writes a local receipt and throws on failure; audioCaptured=false documents that this fixture never opened real inputs.

files.role: Swaps the workspace for a plain cover without stopping ongoing transcription or answers, while narrowing fresh UI Automation traversal.

blocks.title: Start uncovered and keep a single explicit toggle
blocks.explanation: The partial window tracks only visual cover state, prior keyboard focus and a transition guard. InitializeCover detaches the unused CoverView so the initial visual and automation tree contains the normal workspace. The top-bar button toggles this state; there is no recorder detection, startup recording or implicit model request.

blocks.title: Refuse unsafe transitions and detach the real workspace
blocks.explanation: Repeated/reentrant state changes return. Entering cover is refused while file I/O, unsaved confirmation or protection recovery is pending, preserving actionable UI. The code captures workspace focus, clears keyboard/logical focus, disables the workspace and removes it from its host before attaching CoverView. The named controls and data remain alive for asynchronous updates. No stop, cancel, Hide or provider reconfiguration method is called.

blocks.title: Restore the visual tree and rebuild the window's automation children
blocks.explanation: Uncover removes CoverView and restores/enables WorkspaceRoot. The icon remains unchanged; a two-unit border marks covered state and accessible names describe showing the notepad or restoring the workspace without visible text captions. ResetChildrenCache synchronously rebuilds the window peer children, then invalidates peer state. Cached references and retained memory remain outside this fresh-tree improvement. finally releases the transition guard.

blocks.title: Resume layout and visible timing without restarting work
blocks.explanation: After the transition guard is cleared, uncover recalculates layout, queues existing device-card layout and renders the latest answer. Prior keyboard focus is restored only if the element is still visible, enabled and focusable, and never during synthetic rendering. Nothing restarts audio or resubmits a question; text received while covered is already in the retained controls/models.

files.role: Exercises synthetic cover appearance, retained background work and explicitly limited accessibility-tree privacy.

blocks.title: Gate a fake answer until the cover is active
blocks.explanation: The fake provider signals acceptance without yielding text, then waits on an explicit release gate with the actual request cancellation token. It yields one synthetic delta and terminal completion. This arrangement proves a response can arrive after cover activation without contacting a model, and makes erroneous cancellation observable.

blocks.title: Traverse an existing WPF automation peer tree with a bound
blocks.explanation: A queue walks GetChildren from the window peer and refuses more than4096peers. The test can compare references obtained before and after detachment, rather than treating hidden pixels as accessibility proof. This is in-process provider traversal, not a cross-process screen-reader certification.

blocks.title: Establish meaningful before/after accessibility controls
blocks.explanation: Synthetic note/question text and the delayed provider create content worth hiding. The pre-cover tree must contain the editor peer. A simulated audio-start token/busy flag makes accidental shutdown detectable. Cover must detach visual and logical parents, disable the workspace and hide its fields. Fresh traversal must omit old note/question/answer peers while retaining the cover message and toggle. A separate cached-value probe records whether a saved peer still reads retained text, explicitly exposing the limitation.

blocks.title: Continue transcript and answer work without false visible timing
blocks.explanation: The cover blocks an accidental workspace shortcut. A current-session synthetic transcript final arrives and the fake answer is released; completion, unchanged original draft/note/source/session and an uncancelled start token are required. No extra snapshot is created. First-visible logging must remain false while detached. All themes must keep the cover label/toggle visible and omit synthetic private values from fresh traversal.

blocks.title: Inspect real cover-message pixels, minimum geometry and unchanged HWND
blocks.explanation: The synthetic WPF render is sampled within the actual DPI-scaled text bounds; more than100bright pixels prove the message was drawn rather than trusting IsVisible alone. Minimum-size geometry must leave the message/toggle visible. HWND/styles/protection remain unchanged through cover. Uncover must restore the answer text and ordinary editor traversal and then record its first visible assignment.

blocks.title: Preserve editing and device setup and refuse file-busy cover
blocks.explanation: The fake audio-start guard is cleared before further UI checks. Independent question editing survives a cover cycle. Audio setup also restores its selected output/microphone objects without visibility callbacks closing it or reconfiguring work during host swaps. File-busy activation is rejected. Synthetic content/provider mode is then cleared and normal fixture state restored.

blocks.title: Report bounded evidence rather than universal invisibility
blocks.explanation: The aggregate requires visual, keyboard, background-work, fresh accessibility, compact, HWND, restoration and busy-guard checks. The receipt separately reports cachedPeerValueReadable, zero live model requests and no audio capture. Its limitation explicitly excludes cached external clients, process inspection and recipient capture qualification. Failed checks throw instead of generating a successful privacy claim. The final aggregate also requires an accepted native Peek-prevention request; actual taskbar-hover output is not tested.

blocks.title: Assert the icon-only top-left mask target
blocks.explanation: The helper checks that button content is the actual vector Path with geometry, not a string caption. Its top-left coordinates must stay within the header inset, and its target remains32by32. Native hit testing at its center must report client content rather than caption dragging. Covered and restored modes both run this assertion; the separate drag check moved to an unobstructed header point.
